I. 
INTRODUCTION 
A. 
SUMMARY 
In this Decision, the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (Authority or PURA) 
establishes the inflation-adjusted amount of community access support required pursuant 
to General Statutes § 16-331a(k). The consumer price index (CPI)1 for the 2023 inflation 
rate is 2.59%. The Authority uses this number to determine the 2024 inflation-adjusted 
amounts of community access support required from all multichannel video programming 
distributors. 
B. 
BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING 
The General Assembly requires the provision of “facilities, equipment, and 
technical and managerial support to enable the production of meaningful community 
access programming within [each] franchise area.” General Statutes § 16-331a(b). 
Through an annual proceeding, the Authority determines “the amount that the company 
or organization responsible for community access operations shall receive for such 
operations from subscribers and from multichannel video programming distributors.” 
General Statutes § 16-331a(k). 
Holders of a Certificate of Cable Franchise Authority (CCFA) or Certificate of Video 
Franchise Authority (CVFA) are required to provide funds in the amount established by 
the Authority. 
C. 
CONDUCT OF THE PROCEEDING 
On its own motion, the Authority established this docket on January 26, 2024. The 
Authority delegated this matter to its Office of Education, Outreach, and Enforcement 
(EOE). Notice of Proceeding, p. 1. 
EOE filed a motion to approve a Proposed Final Decision on April 11, 2024. 
Participants had seven days from the filing of EOE’s motion to review the proposed 
decision and to file objections to the motion. 
On April 25, 2024, the Authority issued a Proposed Final Decision. All participants 
were given the opportunity to file written exceptions to the Proposed Final Decision. 
Exceptions were filed by numerous community access providers and letters in lieu were 
filed by multichannel video programming distributors (MVPD). Pursuant to Conn. 
Agencies Regs. § 16-331a-10(b), MVPDs have 30 days after notification of the adjusted 
amount per subscriber if they believe the calculation is incorrect. 
D. 
PARTICIPANTS AND INTERVENORS 
The Authority designated the Office of Consumer Counsel (OCC), Ten Franklin 
Square, New Britain, Connecticut 06051; the Commissioner of the Department of Energy 

1 Conn. Agencies Regs. § 16-331a-1(2) defines the consumer price index as the United States Department 
of Labor Consumer Price Index, Urban Northeast Region, published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. 

Docket No. 24-01-06 

Page 2 

and Environmental Protection (DEEP Commissioner) 79 Elm Street, Hartford, 
Connecticut 06106; EOE, Ten Franklin Square, New Britain, Connecticut 06051, and all 
Connecticut MVPDs and community access providers as participants to this proceeding. 
All Connecticut cable advisory councils were designated intervenors. A listing of all 
participants and intervenors is appended hereto as Appendix C.2 
II. 
STANDARD OF REVIEW 
By June 1 of each year, PURA establishes the amount of funding for community 
access operations for each franchise area. General Statutes § 16-331a(k); Conn. 
Agencies Regs. § 16-331a-10. The amount of funding is determined by adjusting the 
prior year amount by the CPI for the preceding calendar year. Id.3 

After considering certain criteria, the Authority may increase or decrease this 
amount within a range of 40% of the inflation adjusted subscriber fee. Id. When 
evaluating whether to increase or decrease the per-subscriber amount, the Authority shall 
consider the factors articulated in Conn. Agencies Regs. § 16-331a-8. 
III. 
AUTHORITY ANALYSIS 
A. 
CPI CALCULATION 

The Authority determines herein: (1) the 2023 rate of inflation as measured by the 
CPI for the Northeast Urban Region; (2) the 2024 franchise-specific community access 
support per subscriber amounts; and (3) whether the amounts are within +/-40% of the 
allowed statutory amount, as adjusted for inflation. 
The index values for determining the rate of inflation for 2023 as measured by the 
CPI4 for the Northeast Urban Region are as follows: 
Year 
Dec. 
2022 
308.150 
2023 
316.143 

Based on this data, the 2023 rate of inflation for updating community access 
support amounts pursuant to General Statutes § 16-331a(k) is 2.59%. Since the CPI for 
the Northeast Urban Region increased 2.59% during 2023, the community access 
support amounts are increased by 2.59% as shown in Appendix A. To determine the +/-
40% range within which the Authority may change the per subscriber amount, the 
Authority adjusts the original statutory $5 per subscriber, as adjusted yearly, by the 
inflation adjustment. In the 2023 Decision, the Authority found that the statutory amount 
as adjusted for inflation was $10.82. Increasing this amount by 2.59% for 2023 CPI 

2 The Authority requests that all participants inform the Authority of any changes/additions to the names, 
addresses and /or titles in the Appendix C service list by filing correspondence in this docket. 
3 The General Assembly set the initial amount at five dollars per subscriber per year. 
4 See https://www.bls.gov/regions/mid-atlantic/data/consumerpriceindexhistorical_northeast_table.htm. 

Docket No. 24-01-06

inflation equates to a value of $11.10. Forty percent of $11.10 is $4.44. Consequently, 
the community access support per subscriber must be between $6.66 ($11.10 – $4.44) 
and $15.54 ($11.10 + $4.44). Appendix A demonstrates that the subscriber amounts are 
properly within this range. 
For the MVPDs “the amount shall be paid on a quarterly basis and shall be 
determined by multiplying the amount per subscriber by the average number of 
subscribers as determined in section 16-331a-9.” Conn. Agencies Regs. § 16-331a-7. 
Each MVPD will be ordered to fund community access in 2024 at the inflation-adjusted 
per-subscriber amount shown in Appendix A. 
B. 
REQUESTS FOR INCREASE 
In this docket, the Authority does not order an increase beyond the CPI of last 
year’s total figure for each MVPD as set forth in Appendix A. Many community access 
providers requested that the Authority increase their subscriber fees to the $15.54 
maximum allowed within the 40% range. See, e.g. Branford Community Television 
Written Exceptions, May 8, 2024, p. 1. Many of the community access providers also 
provided numbers showing that the amount the community access providers received in 
funding through subscriber fees has been declining in recent years, other than 2022 
when the Authority ordered an increase. See, e.g., Totoket TV Written Exceptions, p. 2. 
Conversely, Charter Communications of Northeastern Connecticut and Charter 
Communications of Western Connecticut (Charter) states that the level of support 
provided in the Western Connecticut area has “exceeded that necessary to support 
meaningful community access” and requests an order for Charter to engage in informal 
discussions with EOE to consider the surcharge level going forward. Charter Written 
Exceptions, p. 1. 
The Authority declines to exercise its discretion to further adjust the subscriber fee 
in this year’s annual docket as the records lacks substantial evidence on which to base 
such a decision, and because PURA has received no further legislative direction to do 
so. The Authority also declines to issue an order as requested by Charter.5 
IV. 
CONCLUSION AND ORDERS 
A. 
CONCLUSION 
The increase in the CPI for the Northeast Urban Region during calendar year 2023 
is 2.59%. The franchise-specific inflation adjustments calculated in this Decision apply to 
all Connecticut MVPDs and community access providers. The 2024 Subscriber Fee 
required of each MVPD is set forth in Appendix A. 

5 Charter, like all participants, may engage in discussions with EOE (which is also a participant in these 
proceedings) without an order from the Authority. 

Docket No. 24-01-06 

Page 4 

B. 
ORDERS 
For the following Orders, participants shall file electronic versions through the 
Authority’s website at www.ct.gov/pura. Submissions filed in compliance with the 
Authority’s Orders must be identified by all three of the following: Docket Number, Title 
and Order Number. Compliance with orders shall commence and continue as indicated 
in each specific Order or until a participant requests and the Authority approves that the 
compliance is no longer required after a certain date. Unless otherwise provided or 
determined by the Authority, filings submitted in compliance with an order shall constitute 
satisfaction of the order. Filings requiring Authority approval must be filed as a motion. 
1. 
Effective July 1, 2024, and continuing for twelve (12) months, each MVPD shall 
fund community access using the 2024 Subscriber Fee shown in Appendix A for 
each franchise service area in which it provides video service. Frontier shall fund 
community access using the 2024 Subscriber Fee shown in Appendix A for each 
franchise service area in which it provides video service, and shall file, as a 
compliance filing, the Subscriber Fee and total amount paid for each franchise 
service area in which it provides service. 
2. 
All Advisory Councils shall file their 2024 Annual Report no later than January 31, 
2025, under the current Docket Number. 
3. 
All Community Access Providers shall file their 2024 Community Access Report 
no later than February 15, 2025, under the current Docket Number. 
4. 
The designated community access providers, advisory councils, parties, 
intervenors, and MVPDs shall inform the Authority of any changes/additions to the 
names, addresses and /or titles in the Appendix C service list.
